inputs_used: content-system/seo/link-map.csv (grep: seating, guest list, micro wedding, interactive, timeline, concierge, magazine)

payload.title: Wedding Without a Seating Chart and How to Make It Work
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s planning a luxury or destination wedding, who are tempted to skip the seating chart and want an honest answer on whether that will work for their guest list, reception style and family, and how to make open or partial seating feel considered rather than chaotic across a wedding weekend.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about planning a destination wedding (single primary CTA, placed after the destination weddings across several days section); /magazine as a soft secondary link in the close.
payload.angle: Page-one results either cheer for no seating chart or warn against it. We give an honest answer to 'is a seating chart necessary?': when skipping it works (small or micro weddings, cocktail or food-station receptions, relaxed welcome dinners) and when it doesn't (plated dinners, large guest lists, family tensions, mobility or dietary needs, venues that need table numbers), then show how to make open or partial seating feel considered at a luxury wedding (reserved tables for the couple, family and elders; assigning tables not seats; stations, long tables and lounges). The destination layer is ours: across a wedding weekend, an open welcome dinner and an assigned wedding dinner can sit side by side, with venue layout and service rules framed as questions to ask. Advice only, no statistics and no figures.
must_include: Intro, then exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways

Is a seating chart necessary: when skipping it works (small or micro weddings, cocktail or food-station receptions, relaxed welcome dinners) and when it doesn't (plated dinners, large guest lists, family tensions, mobility or dietary needs, venues that need table numbers); link /what-is-a-micro-wedding once here
Prominent links to /expert-advice/wedding-seating-chart and /expert-advice/how-to-make-a-wedding-seating-chart, framed as 'if you decide you want one'

Ways to make it work: open seating with reserved tables for the couple, family and elders; assign tables not seats; cocktail or food stations; long tables; lounges; link /expert-advice/11-interactive-wedding-ideas-your-guests-will-love once

Practical details: enough seats plus spares framed as a question to ask the venue (no numbers); signage and the MC's announcement; dietary and allergy needs agreed with the caterer (Food Standards Australia New Zealand linked inline only if an allergen claim is made); accessible seating and sightlines; order of the day with /expert-advice/wedding-day-timeline linked once; /expert-advice/how-to-make-a-wedding-guest-list and /wedding-guest-list-template linked once each

Destination weddings across several days: open welcome dinner, assigned wedding dinner; venue layout and service rules framed as questions to ask; single primary CTA to /wonderland-concierge after this section

Close with one Wedded Advisor line using brand-facts.md confirmed claims only (for example one Wedded Advisor start to finish as a single point of contact, planning venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world), linking /wonderland-concierge and /magazine
avoid: Statistics or figures of any kind: 'most couples', percentages, guest-count thresholds, spare-seat numbers, prices (person's decision)
Vendor names or links to vendor pages; seating chart tool or app names (including the Prismm comparison page)
Competitor wording, claims or images (no Easy Weddings or other competitor copy)
Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md confirmed claims: no rates, commissions, availability, named Advisor, or Wedded Privileges
Non-official sources; any allergen or accessibility claim stated without the official source linked inline at the claim
Research talk in the copy (sources, method, what we could or couldn't find)
Title or meta title as a question, with colons or dashes, or over 60 characters
payload.content_format: Guide (fixed by person): honest answer, when it works and when it doesn't, ways to make it work, practical details, destination weekend, FAQ
payload.regional_scope_reason: Seating advice is universal and the grouped search demand is mostly US; the only Australia-specific element is the allergen source (Food Standards Australia New Zealand), which is linked only if needed. SEO to test global versus au_focus.
payload.cannibalisation_check: No existing page targets 'wedding without seating chart'. /expert-advice/wedding-seating-chart and /expert-advice/how-to-make-a-wedding-seating-chart own the head term and the how-to intent; this post owns the counter-question ('is a seating chart necessary', 'no seating plan') and links to both prominently rather than repeating them. /expert-advice/prismm-vs-wonderland-studio is a tool comparison in the same cluster and is not linked here (tool names avoided). SEO to confirm the two seating chart pages' target keywords do not include 'no seating chart'.
